framing: CBT-informed peer-support facilitation — psychoeducation and structured noticing, not clinical CBT therapy or diagnosis.
source_note: Original prompts/experiments informed by screened OpenAlex literature (docs/cbt-informed-research.md). Not copied worksheets; not a claim that Small Circles delivers CBT therapy.

prompts.text: What was happening just before things felt hardest this week — where were you, and what was going on around you?
prompts.rationale: Separates situation from interpretation without diagnosing.

prompts.text: When that hard moment showed up, what thought went through your mind, and what feeling came with it?
prompts.rationale: Links thoughts and feelings as noticing practice, not pathology labels.

prompts.text: Where do you notice this showing up in your body or energy (for example tension, fatigue, restlessness)?
prompts.rationale: Grounds reflection in present-moment cues without clinical assessment.

prompts.text: What is one interpretation of this situation that feels heavy — and is there another way to describe the same facts that feels a little more balanced or kind?
prompts.rationale: Gentle reappraisal framed as optional perspective-taking, not correcting the user.

prompts.text: If a friend were in your exact situation, what would you want them to hear — without fixing them?
prompts.rationale: Self-compassion via perspective shift; avoids toxic positivity.

prompts.text: Of everything weighing on you, what is one small piece that is at least partly within your control this week?
prompts.rationale: Supports agency without implying the user can control everything.

prompts.text: Was there anything — even briefly — that made things 5% more manageable this week?
prompts.rationale: Notices helpful conditions and small actions already present.

prompts.text: If you imagined an inch-sized next step (not a full fix), what might it look like — if you chose to try anything at all?
prompts.rationale: Behavioural activation lite; keeps action optional and small.

experiments.text: If it feels manageable, set a 10-minute timer for one valued or restoring activity, then stop when the timer ends.
experiments.rationale: Short BA-style activation with a clear stop rule.

experiments.text: Write down only the next single task (one line). Do that one item, or decide deliberately to postpone it without self-attack.
experiments.rationale: Reduces overwhelm via one concrete next action.

experiments.text: Once today, jot a sticky note: situation / thought / feeling (three short phrases). No need to solve it.
experiments.rationale: Externalises the noticing triangle without clinical homework tone.

experiments.text: Send yourself one kind sentence you would offer a friend in the same spot — aloud or written.
If safe and wanted, send one low-pressure message to someone you trust (even just 'thinking of you').
experiments.rationale: Small connection action aligned with peer-support goals.
